questions_and_answers.question: Relatively small amounts of blood are within the pulmonary circulation (about 18%) and the heart (about 12%). The largest percentage of blood is within the systemic circulation (about 70%), with the greatest amount (about 55%) within the body’s systemic veins. The relatively large amount of blood within these vessels allows them to function as blood reservoirs. Blood may be shifted from these reservoirs in times of increased physical exertion with vasoconstriction. When less blood is needed at rest, it will be shifted back through by vasodilation.
